steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: Welcome, Pepe.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Is this the Shah's treasure trove? It looks so much like the museum...

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: Your instincts are correct. Parts of the city felt familiar, even before my memories returned.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: I believe its architects may have been inspired by the mausoleum.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: What lies here, Zubayr?
The oil lamps on the wall light up, illuminating the hall with rays that meander through the mirror-smooth walls and pillars.
Countless ghostly shadows appear in an orderly procession in the hall.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: So the treasure in the Shah's trove was... himself?

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Was he a narcissist?

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: Of course not. My sister missed Father after he was gone, and she had me preserve his visage here.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: A thousand years ago, historians preserved the words and deeds of my father using ancient technology they discovered, allowing him to appear, in a way.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: I found something similar in Arsalan. It showed me an image of the Shah in a crystal cave.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: I left it as such. I thought a descendant of Nightzmora would find it and follow the trail.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: You hid it too well, Zubayr. No one else could have found it.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: I hid it? I built a massive temple on top of it.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: I guess it didn't stand the test of time. All I found were some ruins.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: But it guided you here, where you awakened me.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: That is the wonder of time. What seemed trivial at the time could, by fate and coincidence, cause the puzzle piece to fall perfectly into place.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: There are even images of the Shah without his mask...

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Arsalan wasn't the only site I've seen images like these. When I was little, while playing hide-and-seek, my brother and I stumbled upon a chamber where the dead lay in their sarcophagi.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: I knew I would have to come into contact with these things eventually, but it was too much for a child of my age.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: In my panic, I accidentally activated a mechanism and an image of the Shah appeared. At the time, I didn't know who he was—just some ghost trying to communicate with me.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: He told me those sarcophagi were history buried in the sand.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: When those from the future dig them up, they will serve as a bridge across the vastness of time, bringing history and the present together over the great river of time.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: I remember the saying... it's what Father said to comfort my sister when our mother passed away.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: I remember what he said to my sister, after she became Historian. You must not...

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: You must not let escape what made those heroes heroes so—each history has its reverse face.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: So you've heard it.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: It was the last thing the image said. I've never forgotten.
Looking upon the image of Lugalszargus, Pepe cannot help but feel a sense of absurdity.
She had spent so much time wondering what the Shah's treasure trove held.
Now, though, she realizes she has been chasing shadow after shadow.
She holds her hammer tight, fighting back the urge to swing it and drive away the visages.
But what she fears more is the notion that perhaps her family's duty and legacy are nothing more than shadows too.

steps.name: Ajani
steps.text: Medjehtiqedti Hanim, I've contacted all your staff in the directory.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: Anyone else crazy enough to come?

steps.name: Ajani
steps.text: I'm not sure. A lot of the answers are very vague...

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: Thank you. Get a few more bottles of water for Anat, please.

steps.name: Ajani
steps.text: At once, Medjehtiqedti Hanim.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: Brave souls like Izaja and Inaja are hard to come by.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: We only have a couple of hours, Anat.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: The best thing we could ask of them is to make a run for it outside the city.

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: Sorry, Titi, but I'm busy comparing the city survey records and I don't have time to think about that.

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: But you know why I stayed. The same reason as you.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: ...Duty.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: What about the two tourists, though? They have nothing to do with Zubayr's reanimation.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: They don't even have much to do with the city. But now we're asking them to go into the sewers, do the most dangerous investigation, and try to block the sand from surging in.

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: Which is why I must do my best, so that their courage isn't wasted.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: ...I'll rub your ears.

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: Thank you, Titi. I needed that.

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: Look, this construction logbook mentions unusual geological structures.

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: I'll mark them down.

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: Say, Titi... I never managed to publish my research on Zubayr, and no one will ever know about our explorations of the subterranean structure of the city...

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: Will Father be disappointed that I died without leaving my 'name' behind?

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: Blame Pepe. Our dear Princess was just too good at her job—

steps.name: Medjehtiqedti
steps.text: —Lazvar Effendi?

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: I apologize, esteemed Overseer, but the museum is not in a position to offer hospitality during this emergency...

steps.name: Lazvar
steps.text: Please, no need for formalities. I'm no longer the Overseer; just a humble craftsman, free again at last.

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: The museum cannot guarantee your safety at this time. We must advise you to leave the city center as soon as possible, by any means possible...

steps.name: Lazvar
steps.text: After I handed everything over, I stood before the flowing sands with Zubayr Effendi for a while.

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: You saw him?!

steps.name: Lazvar
steps.text: I saw him attempt to repair one clay statue after another using Arts, but eventually he stopped and said to me, 'Such is our duty.'

steps.name: Lazvar
steps.text: I understand. Duty is what we uphold to the very end, without ever asking why.

steps.name: Lazvar
steps.text: To whatever end.

steps.name: Lazvar
steps.text: What can I do to save the city?

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Alright, it's time to show my leadership skills. Soon you'll realize that you should've listened to me and stayed in the museum to protect the others—

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: We'll end up where we started if we turn left here.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: ...What the heck is going on? This hasn't happened before, in all my time in these sewers.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Let me just say that I've never gotten lost when leading my crew. This isn't an indicator of my incompetence.

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: I didn't say it was. Perhaps these winding passages were designed to confuse your sense of direction.

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: I overheard part of the conversation as the museum curators were perusing the survey records.

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: They believe these old sewers are just a small part of the city's underground structures, and they might be able to deduce a path to the deeper levels through historical records.

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: They had been assisting an archaeologist, trying to find clues that may lead to the site known as the 'treasure trove' in ancient documents.

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: If the former site of another massive building really is hidden beneath this city...

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: A treasure trove?

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: ...Forget I said anything.

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: You don't seem afraid.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Afraid of what?

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Isn't our job just to find the sand leak and close the gate to that section? If the gate's broken, we'll just seal it with the boards that we're carrying.

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: There is a good chance we won't find it.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Well... that would be a shame, since the city is getting buried in the sand, if we fail.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: But we'll be the first to see the sand rushing up from deep down, and we may have time to call the museum and warn them to run. We'll be dead for sure, of course.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Wait... is this why you insisted on coming to the sewers?

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Because it's dangerous, and you need to be at the front of it?

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: Narantuya, Aspasia, do you hear me?

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Yeah, we're together.

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: We found a clue.

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: Listen carefully and you should find Lazvar's clockwork fowlbeasts... They're machines that resemble blue fowlbeasts.

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: We've estimated a few possible locations for the deep-level structures. If you can create an opening in the wall, the clockwork fowlbeasts can fly down and gather information.

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: With enough information, we should be able to find exactly where the sand is rushing in. But there is one caveat...

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: The clockwork fowlbeasts are unable to perform heavier tasks like toggling switches and plugging gaps... you will have to go into danger.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: You must have seen it in the memories that I showed you. The circlet you're wearing is the same as my sister's.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: It was passed down through the family.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: I wondered why my family was so obsessed with recording the Shahanshah's history. Father had no answer; he simply said it was our inherent duty.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: But now I see the answer is so simple: it is out of a daughter's longing for her father.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: My sister always believed that he would return, someday.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: She never saw that day. And I never got the chance to say goodbye to her.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: All I had left for company after my sister's death was my father's shadows.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: Leave your obsession with the City of Gold behind, Pepe. I know how to seal consciousness into a gem, and how to build a body that never decays.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: You will have life eternal to experience, to discover, to record...

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: I'm sorry, Zubayr... I can't replace your sister and keep you company.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: I have a younger brother myself. He's the Historian of Shar-Agade.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: A shame. It is hardly an honor. They know too much that cannot be put to paper.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: My foolish brother wanted the historians to document history to his liking, and so he forced my sister to send one of her twin sons into the palace.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: A thousand years later, coercion has become honor.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: The Sovereign of Beasts said all historians will have their tongues cut out. Is that true?

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: I do not know the ways of the current Shahanshah, but it is a proven way to keep a secret.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: I need to go to the City of Gold and find him, no matter what.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: I knew it.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: Then leave, Pepe.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: No... Not yet.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: I can't leave this city to its fate.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: I can't allow the constructs to continue wreaking havoc in the city.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Spare the city. As you said, the most precious treasures have not been defiled.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: I cannot stop, Pepe, even if I wanted to.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: In our lives, we go through many choices, big and small. One links to another, carving out unique circuits for all of us amidst infinite branching paths.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: My oaths to Father and Sister have been etched as circuits, preserved for all eternity upon these gems.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: I can never defy them.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: Never.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Then tell me how to stop the constructs, Zubayr.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: I have already told you the answer. The rest is up to you, Pepe.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: Catch me if you can, like the invading armies so many centuries ago.

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: There's something I've been meaning to tell you, since talking to Ajazi and Ajani the other day.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Man, this is a hard rock. I hope we have enough time... what did they say?
A blue clockwork fowlbeast circles overhead, urging them to dig through the stone bricks before them.
Aspasia is glad that everything is going smoothly. She has only one more task before embarking on the path, if it indeed exists.

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: I learned why you thirst for wealth. You feel like you owe your past crew.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Oh. When did they start? The night when we fled for our lives? Or the time when I gave away all the treasure?

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: After you left.

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: I heard many stories from Ajazi and Ajani—how they struggled to use saws properly while logging, often breaking them with brute force. How they tried their hand at bookkeeping but messed up the records.

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: How someone slaughtered their last burdenbeast with a knife, then sold the knife to buy a pot to treat everyone to a feast.

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: ...Word about his cooking spread, and he opened a food stall at the market. Customers flock to his stall till this very day.

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: How someone wrote a novel based on their time as a desert bandit and became published in the local paper. The latest chapters feature your gang traveling back in time to fight for the Shah's throne.

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: Most of your old crew have a house and don't need to migrate with the seasons. If they fix their roofs in time, they won't even leak during monsoon season. I'd say they're all doing rather well.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: ...Of course I know that.

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: I respect you, but I don't think you owe them anything.

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: Just as you don't have to save an entire city just to save Ajazi and Ajani.

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: You should get out, go back to see them... then put down your burden, your 'duty', and start moving forward again.
Aspasia is interrupted by the rumbling of a sliding boulder.
The pair seems to have stumbled upon one of the mechanisms of the ancient maze; the etched brick retreats into the walls of the canal, and they hear the sound of falling a few seconds later.
The entire wall begins to collapse, but as Anat said, what lies beyond is not sand.
Pitch-black darkness indicates that they are staring at the interior of a massive structure.
There is no path in front of them. The sound of quicksand is clearly audible from deeper in, as though there is a raging river deep in the abyss.
A river from which there is no return.
The pair throw down their pickaxes and draw their weapons at exactly the same time.
Kicking up a cloud of dust, they face off less than ten paces apart.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: What are you doing?

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: Stopping you from jumping down.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Wasn't I the one who had to stop you just now?

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Been wanting to say this, if you came to die, I can't let you go any further.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: I thought you would be better than those two stooges, but it turns out you need me to save you, too.

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: ...I told you, you don't have to carry this burden.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: You've got it wrong. I just want to go down and see for myself. Besides, no one can do it better than me. That's all.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: I want a mountain of gold, even if I didn't care about letting my crew live a better life. I'm just greedy, plain and simple.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: 'In our lives, we go through many choices, big and small.'

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: You call it duty. I prefer to call it my choice. This is who I am.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Right then. You're a trained fighter who won't walk into a knife. Well, things are about to get real this time. Don't get mad.

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: I have nothing but sincere gratitude towards you, Narantuya.

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: I need not fear a duel with you.

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: I didn't dare believe my heart, because I had made an oath to my family... about blood and violence, about war being the most just form of violation.

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: But you've shown me how resolved the heart can be.

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: Perhaps there is something to be said about the convictions of the Sargonians. My choices make me who I am. From this day—

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: —Hey, wait for me to finish!
Her vision goes black.
A black blade fan sweeps past her eyes. She blinks just once, but the only light source has already gone out.
She knows that Narantuya has two black knives. They are equipped with special mechanisms and cannot be unsheathed directly.
Yet in that instant, all she recalls is the Kuranta Elders known as the Nightzmora—renowned for their relentless marching day and night, devouring the sun at high noon.
She charges at where her counterpart should be, relying on her memory—
—And comes up empty.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: A little sleight of sand, a simple mirage of Originium Arts.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Who said anything about winning the fight? All I need to do is jump first.
Embraced by darkness and illusion, Narantuya takes a step back.

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: Wait, Narantuya! This is not a fair duel!

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Another silver medal for you.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Are you serious, Zubayr?

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: You're instructing me to attack you, and moving like the wind at the same time.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: Give up, Pepe. I told you, it's futile.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: You can never touch me, no matter how hard you swing that hammer of yours.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Hmph, I'll show you!

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: Are you trying to break the support beams to limit my movements?

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: Again, it's futile.
The broken columns and floor are quickly repaired by sand, leaving no trace of damage.
Pepe goes through illusion after illusion, seeking Zubayr.
Whenever she catches a glimpse, however, he soon disappears behind more illusions and is once again nowhere to be seen.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: Focus, Pepe.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Did you know, Zubayr?

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Before I turned fourteen, the doctors said I was a frail girl who would never lift a heavy hammer like this.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: Quite the difference, the way you're swinging it, despite your diminutive figure.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: I trained under Sargon's top strongman so that I could penetrate the deserts and jungles, and discover long-lost ancient ruins.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: By the age of seventeen, I could cross the vast desert on my own, and fight off a dozen bandits at the same time.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: That alone is not enough, Pepe.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: I'm not trying to prove myself to you.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: I'm just telling you, there has never been anything I couldn't do, if I put my mind to it.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: No matter how hard, how out of reach... as long as I mean it...

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: I can do it!

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: You hold this impression because you have only lived twenty-two years.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: I had cut down countless foes with my sword when I fought under my father's banner.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: Their screams filled me with confidence. I believed that there was nothing I couldn't acquire, nothing I couldn't do, given enough time.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: Little did I know, that my greatest enemy... was time itself!
A golden flash, and Pepe feels an intense pain from her ankle before she could turn around.
The staff is much heavier than expected.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: You must be faster, Pepe.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: It is etched upon my gem circuit that everyone who violates my father's tomb must die.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: Your attacks have begun to anger it.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: It is urging me to put an end to it all.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: You should not have played this game with me, Zubayr.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: This is not a game, Pepe.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: No, it is...

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: You closed your eyes?
Nothing but darkness. Pepe knows that her eyes aren't fast enough and will only hold her back.
She could never catch her agile brother when playing hide-and-seek in the garden. He was like a slippery fin.
Until one day, she closed her eyes, and realized she could hear every footstep her brother made on the stone tiles.

a.text: 'I'm ready, sis! Come look for me!'

steps.text: He's right behind me...
If I turn around quick enough...

a.text: 'Why did you close your eyes? Are you admitting defeat?'

steps.text: I can catch him.
Mustering all her might, Pepe turns and swings her hammer. Sure enough, she hears the sound of shattering.
